name: teampcp-campaign-iocs-2026-03-28
description: Campaign-specific IOCs for the TeamPCP (March 2026) multi-ecosystem supply chain attack. Covers compromised action SHAs, malicious package versions/hashes, C2 domains/IPs, persistence artifacts, and actor markers. Structural detections (CI trust, credential sweep, persistence commands) have been promoted to built-in rules and are not repeated here.

rules.title: Known compromised trivy-action commit SHA
rules.description: Detected SHA fragment tied to the TeamPCP trivy-action compromise window.
rules.remediation: Replace this action reference with a commit SHA outside the known compromise window. Re-run pipelines with a vetted trivy-action pin and rotate any secrets reachable from affected workflows.

rules.title: High-risk action reference pinned by tag
rules.description: References one of the compromised action repos by mutable tag instead of immutable commit SHA.

rules.title: Potentially malicious Trivy version reference
rules.description: Version references include trivy 0.69.4, 0.69.5, or 0.69.6 from the compromise period.
rules.remediation: Upgrade to a vendor-supported Trivy release and verify the binary digest against official published checksums. Re-image any runner or container that used the bad versions.

rules.title: Mirror cache reference from compromise timeline
rules.description: mirror.gcr.io references were relevant to persistence of compromised Trivy images after takedown.

rules.title: Known CanisterWorm npm scope
rules.description: Found package scope tied to the TeamPCP npm self-propagation campaign.
rules.remediation: Remove these packages from lockfiles and dependencies. Run npm audit, clear caches, and install only from an allowlisted private registry with namespace controls.

rules.title: CanisterWorm campaign marker
rules.description: CanisterWorm marker associated with credential theft and downstream npm package infection.

rules.title: ICP C2 indicator
rules.description: Found indicator for blockchain-backed C2 infrastructure used during the campaign.

rules.title: Malicious LiteLLM version reference
rules.description: Found references to litellm 1.82.7 or 1.82.8, the compromised versions.
rules.remediation: Pin litellm to a known-good version and reinstall from PyPI with hash verification. Rotate API keys that may have passed through the compromised build.

rules.title: Known malicious LiteLLM wheel hash
rules.description: Detected hash of compromised litellm wheel from the campaign IOC list.
rules.remediation: Delete wheels matching these hashes and reinstall litellm from a trusted index. Verify future installs with pip hash-checking mode or locked requirements.

rules.title: LiteLLM .pth persistence artifact
rules.description: litellm_init.pth indicates possible auto-execution persistence tied to the compromise.
rules.remediation: Remove the .pth file and any site-packages hooks it loaded. Rebuild the environment from a clean virtualenv and scan for further Python persistence.

rules.title: Compromised OpenVSX extension ast-results v2.53.0
rules.description: Detected extension/version combination associated with the campaign.
rules.remediation: Uninstall this extension version and install a publisher-verified build. Review IDE settings and clear extension caches on affected workstations.

rules.title: Compromised OpenVSX extension cx-dev-assist v1.7.0
rules.description: Detected extension/version combination associated with the campaign.
rules.remediation: Remove the compromised extension version and reinstall only after verifying the publisher checksum. Hunt for credential access from affected developer machines.

rules.title: OpenVSX exfiltration endpoint indicator
rules.description: Detected checkmarx.zone/vsx endpoint associated with extension-based exfiltration.

rules.title: sysmon.py persistence file path
rules.description: Detected TeamPCP persistence filename in filesystem path.
rules.remediation: Delete the file and isolate the host for forensic review. Rotate credentials and check systemd, cron, and shell profiles for related persistence.

rules.title: pgmon service persistence file path
rules.description: Detected TeamPCP pgmon persistence file in filesystem path.
rules.remediation: Remove the payload tree and user systemd units referencing it. Reimage or restore from backup and validate no outbound connections to known IOCs.

rules.title: pgmon systemd unit path
rules.description: Detected TeamPCP pgmon systemd unit in filesystem path.
rules.remediation: Disable and delete the unit, then run systemctl --user daemon-reload. Audit remaining user services and timers for copycat persistence.

rules.title: Windows startup lock file indicator
rules.description: msbuild.exe.lock indicates prior execution of TeamPCP telnyx persistence logic.
rules.remediation: Remove the lock file and inspect Startup folders and Run keys for msbuild-based persistence. Perform antivirus and EDR sweeps on the account.

rules.title: TeamPCP payload or tooling artifact
rules.description: Detected known TeamPCP artifact paths and payload names.

rules.title: Malicious telnyx version reference
rules.description: Found references to telnyx 4.87.1 or 4.87.2, the compromised versions.
rules.remediation: Pin telnyx to a clean release and reinstall with hash verification. Revoke API keys that may have been exposed to the compromised package.

rules.title: Known malicious telnyx package hash
rules.description: Detected hash of compromised telnyx source distribution from IOC list.
rules.remediation: Remove sdists or wheels with these hashes and rebuild from PyPI with trusted pins. Block outbound C2 associated with the campaign at the network layer.

rules.title: WAV steganography artifact name
rules.description: Detected known WAV payload artifacts used for steganographic delivery.

rules.title: telnyx campaign C2 endpoint
rules.description: Detected known telnyx payload delivery or exfiltration endpoint.
rules.remediation: Block the IP and URL at egress firewalls and proxies. Hunt for processes or scripts that fetch WAV payloads and remove them along with related Python hooks.

rules.title: Trivy typosquat C2 domain
rules.description: Detected scan.aquasecurtiy.org IOC.
rules.remediation: Sinkhole or block this typosquat domain in DNS and TLS inspection. Search logs for outbound connections and rotate any credentials sent to it.

rules.title: Checkmarx campaign C2 domain
rules.description: Detected checkmarx.zone IOC.
rules.remediation: Deny this domain unless explicitly approved; it was used as C2 in the campaign. Review endpoints and extensions that contacted it and treat hosts as potentially compromised.

rules.title: LiteLLM campaign C2 domain
rules.description: Detected models.litellm.cloud IOC.
rules.remediation: Block this domain and audit LiteLLM configs for unexpected model endpoints. Rotate API keys used with LiteLLM integrations.

rules.title: Campaign infrastructure domain IOC
rules.description: Detected hackmoltrepeat.com IOC.

rules.title: Campaign infrastructure IP IOC
rules.description: Detected known TeamPCP campaign IP IOC.

rules.title: Exfiltration repository IOC
rules.description: Detected tpcp-docs/docs-tpcp repository marker used for fallback exfiltration.
rules.remediation: Remove references to these staging repositories from workflows and scripts. Revoke tokens that could push or read from them and verify no data was exfiltrated.

rules.title: Exfiltration bundle marker
rules.description: Detected campaign exfil bundle marker tpcp.tar.gz or matching HTTP header.
rules.remediation: Treat this archive marker as exfil: block uploads containing it, inspect HTTP proxies for matching traffic, and rotate credentials packaged in developer environments.

rules.title: Suspicious C2/exfil curl command
rules.description: Detected curl command targeting known TeamPCP C2 or exfil infrastructure.

rules.title: Trivy v0.69.4 malicious binary hash from SANS report
rules.description: Detected SHA256 hash matching one of the backdoored Trivy v0.69.4 binaries documented in the March 2026 incident report.
rules.remediation: Quarantine binaries with these digests and replace them with official Trivy releases from the vendor. Assume breach and rotate CI secrets on any runner that executed them.

rules.title: Compromised Checkmarx/OpenVSX package hash
rules.description: Detected SHA256 hash tied to compromised OpenVSX payload packages in the TeamPCP cascade.
rules.remediation: Delete VSIX or artifacts matching these hashes and reinstall extensions from trusted sources. Review IDE sync and extension auto-update settings on affected machines.

rules.title: CanisterWorm payload hash
rules.description: Detected SHA256 hash corresponding to documented CanisterWorm payload waves.
rules.remediation: Remove npm packages or artifacts with these hashes from registries and caches. Run organization-wide npm integrity checks and revoke publish tokens used during the incident window.

rules.title: Malicious entrypoint hash IOC
rules.description: Detected malicious entrypoint.sh hash from TeamPCP incident documentation.

rules.title: Additional TeamPCP staging server IOC
rules.description: Detected additional campaign staging/source IP documented in cross-vendor forensic reporting.

rules.title: Known TeamPCP Cloudflare relay subdomain
rules.description: Detected one of the trycloudflare relay hostnames observed in TeamPCP payload infrastructure.

rules.title: TeamPCP Kubernetes DaemonSet marker
rules.description: Detected DaemonSet names linked to TeamPCP persistence or destructive components.
rules.remediation: Delete these DaemonSets and review RBAC that allowed their creation. Rotate cluster credentials and scan nodes for destructive payloads tied to the campaign.

rules.title: TeamPCP actor/tool account marker
rules.description: Detected actor or compromised service account names tied to incident timeline and exfiltration operations.
